newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Supreme Court delays ruling on Gonzalez.
newsitem.headline: Spain Supreme Court delays ruling on Gonzalez.

text.p: Spain's Supreme Court on Thursday delayed a decision on whether to question former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez about a 1980s "dirty war" against Basque ETA separatists, local media reported.

Families of the victims had appealed against an April ruling by a single Supreme Court justice that there were no grounds to question Gonzalez in connection with the 1983-87 campaign of killings, kidnappings and bombings in which 27 people died.
Former security chiefs and a disgruntled former Basque region leader of the Socialist party have accused Gonzalez of authorising the campaign against ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).
Gonzalez's Socialist party lost a general election in March after 13 years in power, discredited by the "dirty war" allegations and mounting corruption scandals.

The Supreme Court judge in charge of probing the anti-ETA campaign, Eduardo Moner, ruled in April there was not sufficient hard evidence to warrant questioning Gonzalez and he subsequently refused to hear appeals by the victims' families against the decision.
The full court told Moner on Thursday that the appeals must be heard.
The appeals process is expected to take about a month after which the court will decide whether to call Gonzalez to testify.

Gonzalez's first interior minister, Jose Barrionuevo, is trial on charges of creating and funding anti-ETA death squads. Some 800 people have died in ETA's campaign for Basque independence since 1968.
